title.narrative: Fanikisha Mjane (Ensuring the Success of a Widow)

description.narrative: Fanikisha Mjane is a widow-centred agricultural empowerment project that seeks to strengthen the economic resilience and social dignity of 150 widows living in Ganze Sub-County, Kilifi County. Ganze is widely recognized as a marginalized area where poverty and Gender-Based Violence have become part of daily life, especially for widows. Many of them have been victims of economic exclusion, land disinheritance, social stigma, and sexual abuse. Many remarry out of desperation for safety and economic support, but instead find themselves in abusive relationships. Shockingly, when these widows remarry in search of safety and support, their daughters are often exposed to incestuous abuse by stepfathers, stepbrothers, or male relatives in the new household. These violations are shrouded in silence, sustained by fear, shame, and entrenched cultural norms. Because they are forced to rely on abusive remarried partners for basic survival and acceptance within their communities, these widows feel they have no voice and are compelled to remain in toxic relationships and conform to societal expectations where they have no choice but to sacrifice their dignity, their autonomy, and the safety of their children in the process. The project aims to break this cycle by economically empowering widows through climate smart cassava farming. Cassava farming is well-suited to Ganze’s dry conditions and valued both culturally and also for its high nutritional and commercial value. Widows will receive Page 3 of 14 hands-on training in sustainable cassava production, covering key areas such as land preparation, pest and disease management, organic methods, soil conservation, and post-harvest techniques. These skills will improve productivity while promoting environmentally responsible farming. To further support income generation, the project will establish two community-based cassava processing hubs where widows will engage in value addition, producing products such as flour, crisps, porridge mix, and livestock feed. They will also be trained in product development, branding, packaging, and food safety compliance to help them compete in formal markets. These skills will enhance the marketability and quality of their products, allowing them to meet the demands of institutional buyers such as local hotels, supermarkets, and other retail outlets within Kilifi County and beyond.
